On Fri, 07 Aug 2027 at 16:45 +01:00, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben / Laura — forwarding ThorTech's package. Key asks below (from Sam): controller/processor confirmation, evidence list (KMS/encryption/georouting), and whether we require a Transfer Impact Addendum or can accept standard SCCs.

Thanks — I pulled the redline and did a quick pass. High-level position:

1) Roles: the MSA/order form as currently drafted treats Redwood as processor for customer data and controller for analytics/telemetry. ThorTech has flagged two order-form fields where their proposed language would expand their controller claims. We should: accept the standard processor footprint, and push back on any language that adds controller duties for product telemetry. I'll draft a clean markup focusing on clause X.3 (data responsibilities) and X.7 (audit rights) and propose clarifying language that references the Order Form exhibit.

2) SCCs vs TIA: we should offer the SCCs with a short Transfer Impact Addendum limited to the KMS/exemptions language (if ThorTech insists on customer-managed keys). If ThorTech intends to require customer-managed KMS for production, that has infra and pricing implications — flag to Product and Ops. Otherwise we can sign standard SCCs plus a short addendum confirming geo-routing commitments and cross-border subprocessors list.

3) Evidence bundle (Laura): Ops can produce the following items within 3 business days:
   - KMS architecture diagram (redacted)
   - Confirmation of encryption at rest with key rotation cadence (1-pg summary)
   - Sample token-level audit summary (anonymized)
   - Current subprocessor roster (csv)

4) Risk flags: ThorTech's redline includes a carve-in for training data retention that conflicts with our retention policy; recommend redline to limit retention to specific logs & telemetry for X days and require separate consent for model training.

I'll draft the redline language this weekend and send back a proposed DPA/Order Form tidy-up. Marissa — if procurement asks for an exec-level exception (e.g., to accept their expanded controller wording), flag it and we'll escalate.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_DPA_markup.docx (will follow)

Hi Sam / Jeff —

Thanks for the package and for the clear timeline. Quick update and proposed plan:

- Redwood will provide an initial counter-redline to the DPA and targeted clarifications in the Order Form by EOD Tuesday (10 Aug). Ben is leading the legal markup; I'll send the clean redline to you for review.

- Ops (Laura) will assemble the evidence bundle: KMS architecture sketch, encryption/rotation summary, anonymized audit snapshot, and subprocessor list. We will provide those as redacted PDFs (attachments) and a 1-page summary for your privacy reviewers by Wednesday (11 Aug).

- SCCs: our preferred route is to sign the standard EU SCCs and include a short Transfer Impact Addendum limited to geo-routing assurances and an explicit KMS approach if you require customer-managed keys. If you confirm that standard SCCs suffice, we can avoid a longer TIA.

Attached for transparency: a short execution timeline and a placeholder DocuSign link we'll use once redlines are settled. If ThorTech's procurement needs a PO or subscription order number to process billing before signature, please send it and we'll align.

Action items for ThorTech: please confirm whether you insist on customer-managed keys in prod, and whether the training-data retention carve is negotiable. If you can confirm both by EOD Tuesday we should be able to meet your 14 Aug procurement deadline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
